papers.title_in_file: Time-Spatial Mode Selective Quantum Frequency Converter
papers.version_note: arXiv:2105.14160v1 [quant-ph], dated June 1, 2021; the text layer holds the paper once, 9 pages plus an empty trailing page.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental and simulated demonstration of a sum-frequency-generation quantum frequency converter that selects spatial (Laguerre-Gaussian) and temporal (delay) signal modes with an adaptively optimized pump.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with the pump prepared in optimized modes through adaptive feedback control, selective frequency conversion is demonstrated with up to 30 dB extinction.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Conclusion, Section VI, p.6
quotes: selective frequency conversion is demonstrated with up to 30 dB extinction
high-extinction (up to 30 dB) by selectively upconverting the signal modes using optimized pump
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the 30 dB figure is the upper end of a range in Fig. 7(a).
assertions.reader_inference: The 30 dB figure is the best case. The average selectivities reported in the body are lower: about 28 dB for qubit sets, about 17 and 16 dB for qudit sets, 14 to 15 dB for the spatio-temporal case.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in contrast to a previous demonstration (reference 29), they use an optimized pump beam that is a superposition of many higher-order orthogonal modes, and that they select mutually unbiased basis sets according to their spatial and temporal modes.
quotes: In contrast to previous demonstrations [29], we use an optimized pump beam which is the superposition of many higher-order orthogonal modes.
can be selectively upconverted according to their spatial and temporal modes
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim of novelty relative to cited work.

assertions.value: The authors cite reference 29 as having demonstrated high-dimensional quantum frequency conversion of orbital angular momentum qudits via sum frequency generation with a flat-top Gaussian pump beam.
quotes: HD QFC was demonstrated for orbital angular momentum (OAM) qudits via sum frequency generation (SFG) with a ﬂat-top Gaussian pump beam [29].
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in their model, the full electric field is the product of the spatial and temporal degrees of freedom, so they ignore the inter-coupling of space and time.
quotes: the full electric-ﬁeld is the product of the spatial
we ignore the inter-coupling of the space and
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this modelling assumption in Section II.
assertions.reader_inference: Spatio-temporal coupling is therefore outside the model; the simulation results hold under this separability assumption.

assertions.value: The authors define the normalized sum-frequency (SF) photon number of a signal mode in decibels, relative to the total over all signal modes, with equal input photons for each signal mode. They define the selectivity as the difference between this normalized value for the desired signal mode and that of the other overlapping signal modes.
assertions.anchor: Model, Eqs. 6 and 7, Section II, p.2
quotes: where Ni is the measured SF photons of the ith signal mode and n is the total number of signal modes
the input incident photons for each signal mode are
The selectivity, η, between desired signal mode
are the normalized SF photons of the desired signal and the other overlapping signal modes
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the quantity in Eqs. 6 and 7; the equation layout is garbled in the text layer, so the value restates it in words.
assertions.reader_inference: Selectivity is a ratio of detected up-converted counts expressed in dB, not an absolute conversion efficiency or a state-fidelity measure.

assertions.value: The authors report a simulation with four signal modes in which one optimized pump, found by random-walk optimization, selects signal S4; the selectivity of S4 against S1, S2 and S3 is 20.2 dB, 8.4 dB and 11.8 dB.
quotes: The selectivity of the signal S4 against S1, S2, and S3 are 20.2 dB, 8.4 dB, and 11.8 dB, respectively.
we used a random-walk optimization method to optimize the pump ﬁeld in spatio-temporal domain
assertions.certainty_reason: A single simulated example.
assertions.reader_inference: The spread (8.4 to 20.2 dB) shows the simulated suppression is uneven across the unwanted modes.

assertions.value: The authors report a mode-locked laser giving a pulse train with a pulse width of about 0.3 ps at a repetition rate of 50 MHz, with two 100 GHz-bandwidth wavelength division multiplexers selecting a pump at 1545 nm and a signal at 1558 nm.
quotes: pulse train with pulse width ∼0.3 ps at 50 MHz repetition rate
narrow-band wavelength division multiplexers (WDMs) with bandwidth 100 GHz
one at 1545 nm as a pump and another at 1558 nm as a signal
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the pump pulses are amplified by an erbium-doped fiber amplifier to a maximum average power of about 10 mW on the nonlinear crystal, and that the signal pulses are attenuated with neutral density filters to an ultra-low level.
quotes: maximum average power ∼ 10 mW incident on the nonlinear crystal
the signal optical pulses are attenuated with neutral density ﬁlters to produce ultra-low optical signal
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper gives no signal photon number per pulse in the main text, so the experiment is not stated to be at the single-photon level.

assertions.value: The authors report that the pump and signal beams, with transverse FWHM of 2.8 mm and 2.6 mm (each plus or minus 0.05 mm), are shaped on separate Santec SLM-100 spatial light modulators (1440 by 1050 pixels, pixel pitch 10.4 by 10.4 micrometres), combined on a beam splitter and focused with a focal length of 200 mm.
quotes: The transverse FWHM of the pump and signal are 2.8±0.05 mm and 2.6±0.05 mm, respectively.
Santec SLM-100, 1440 × 1050 pixels, pixel pitch 10.4 × 10.4 µm
focus length F =200 mm
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors report a temperature-stabilized 5 mol.% MgO-doped PPLN crystal with a poling period of 19.36 micrometres, 10 mm long, 3 mm wide and 1 mm high, and state its normalized conversion efficiency as 1%.
quotes: poling period of 19.36 µm (5 mol.% MgO doped PPLN, 10 mm length, 3 mm width, and 1 mm height)
The normalized conversion eﬃciency of the nonlinear crystal is 1%.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper does not define the normalization of the 1% figure in the main text.

assertions.value: The authors report that the output is filtered with a short-pass filter and bandpass filters giving a total of more than 180 dB extinction, and that the visible SF photons are detected by a silicon avalanche photodiode (ID100) with 15% quantum efficiency, read out with an FPGA.
quotes: bandpass ﬁlters to provide a total >180 dB extinction in rejecting
A silicon avalanche photodiode (Si-APD, ID100) is used to detect the photons which has 15% quantum eﬃciency.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The 180 dB extinction applies to rejecting the pump second harmonic (the sentence continues on the next page); it is not a mode-selectivity figure.

assertions.value: The authors state that a MATLAB program optimizes the pump mode using an adaptive feedback technique based on a random-walk optimization, with the SF photons collected by an FPGA and sent to a computer for post processing.
quotes: A MATLAB program is used to optimize the pump mode using adaptive feedback technique based on a random-walk optimization
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors report an experimentally measured matrix of normalized SF output for signal and pump modes with radial index 0 and 1 and azimuthal index from minus 3 to 3. They state that signal and pump modes of opposite angular momentum sign give higher extinction than other modes, and that the nearest neighbour spatial modes are difficult to distinguish.
quotes: both signal and pump modes have the radial index p = 0, 1 and azimuthal index l = −3 to 3
the angular momentum with opposite sign for the signal and pump modes have higher extinction compare to other modes
the nearest neighbour spatial modes are diﬃcult to distinguish
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Neighbouring-mode crosstalk is a stated limit of unoptimized single-LG-mode pumping and motivates the optimized superposition pump.

assertions.value: The authors state that the optimized pump modes are superpositions of 18 higher-order LG modes, with azimuthal index from minus 5 to 5 and radial index 0 or 1.
quotes: The optimized pump modes are in the superposition of the 18 higher-order LG modes (l ∈ [−5 : 5], p ∈ [0, 1]).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own pump basis.
assertions.reader_inference: The index ranges as printed span 11 azimuthal values by 2 radial values, which is 22 combinations rather than 18; the paper does not explain the difference (possibly some combinations are excluded, as an LG mode with p equal to 1 is not listed for every l).

assertions.value: The authors report qubit tomography over two mutually unbiased bases of signal modes, with optimized pump modes selectively picking up the desired modes, achieving selectivity of about 28 dB on average.
quotes: The qubit tomography shows that the optimized pump modes can
selectively pickup the desired modes. It achieves the
selectively of ∼ 28 dB on average.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Selectivity here is the photon-count ratio of the SF output, not a reconstructed-state fidelity; no tomographic fidelity is reported.

assertions.value: The authors report qudit tomography with two sets of four signal modes, each mode selected with its own optimized pump: the first set gives about 17 dB average extinction and the second set, of LG modes with a single LG component each, gives about 16 dB.
quotes: The selectivity η gives ∼17 dB on average
The value of selectivity η gives
∼16 dB extinction.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Selectivity falls from about 28 dB (qubit) to 16 to 17 dB (four-mode qudit), consistent with harder selection as dimension grows; the paper does not state this trend.

assertions.value: The authors report selection among five higher-order LG modes with two different optimized pumps, with selectivity between 20 dB and 30 dB for the first set of five modes and between 15 dB and 25 dB for the second set.
quotes: Figure 7 demonstrates the selectivity among ﬁve higher-order LG modes
the selectivity for 5 signal modes in Fig. 7(a) and (b) are in between 20 dB to 30 dB and 15 dB to 25 dB, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The mode lists in the text and the Fig. 7 caption do not agree with each other in index notation (for example LG02 and LG12 appear beside LG10, LG11); the table values are in an image, so the specific mode labels are not checkable from the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors report an experiment with six signal modes defined in x, y and time, with signal delays of 0 ps, 5 ps, 20 ps, 15 ps, 10 ps and 25 ps relative to the pump; the optimized pumps P1 and P5 gave average selectivities of 15 dB and 14 dB.
quotes: corresponding temporal delays are t0 = 0 ps, 5 ps, 20 ps, 15 ps, 10 ps, and 25 ps, respectively.
The selectivities for P1 and P5 are 15 dB and 14 dB on average, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Only P1 and P5 are reported in the text; pumps for the other four signals are not given. The 15 and 14 dB figures are lower than the purely spatial results. Delays in this experiment are 5 ps or more, much larger than the 0.3 ps pulse width.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the current setup the spatial mode shaping of the pump is provided by the SLM and the temporal shaping is realized by a time delay, and propose that an optical arbitrary waveform generator based on spectral line-by-line pulse shaping could be used in future to manipulate time-frequency modes.
quotes: the spatial mode shaping of the pump is provided by the SLM and the temporal shaping is realized by the time delay
optical arbitrary waveform generator based on spectral line-by-line pulse
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the present limit of its temporal control.
assertions.reader_inference: The temporal dimension is thus a set of delay time bins, not arbitrary temporal-mode (Schmidt-mode) shaping, although Eq. 5 is written with Schmidt decomposed temporal modes.

assertions.value: The authors state that the selectivities can further improve with other efficient adaptive optimization methods, that the selectivity and conversion efficiency can be improved while suppressing intrinsic noise by using a longer nonlinear crystal with a well defined phase matching profile, and that they envision spatio-temporal mode selectivity being effective against channel noise.
assertions.anchor: Results, Section IV, p.5; Discussion, Section V, p.5
quotes: These selectivities can further improve with other eﬃcient adaptive optimization methods
by using longer nonlinear crystal with well deﬁned phase matching proﬁle
We envision that spatio-temporal mode selectivity will be
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statements of expected improvement and use, without evidence in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No channel-noise or entanglement-distribution experiment is reported in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that, thanks to the selectivity among transverse spatial modes, their technique can be used to measure the transverse spatial mode joint probability distribution of a bi-photon state from spontaneous parametric down-conversion, by mode selective measurement on the photon pair separately.
quotes: our technique can be used for measurement of the traverse spatial mode joint probability distribution of a bi-photon state produced in spontaneous parametric down-conversion
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim without evidence in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No bi-photon, entangled or single-photon-level measurement is reported; all counts come from attenuated pulses from a mode-locked laser.

assertions.value: The authors report that rotating the Hermite-Gaussian HG10 phase mask of the pump and the signal, in simulation and experiment, gives minimum SF photons when the pump and signal phase masks are orthogonal to each other.
quotes: It shows that the SF photons are minimum, when the pump and signal phase masks are orthogonal to each other.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the noise photon counts per pulse are about 10 to the power minus 6 (printed as 10−6), less than the noise level attained in an LN waveguide (reference 57), and that the background noise is about 46 dB lower than the up-converted SF photons.
quotes: noise photon counts per pulse is ∼ 10−6, less than the noise level attained in LN waveguide [57]
In this work, the background noise ∼ 46 dB lower than the upconverted SF photons.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The 46 dB noise margin is stated for this measurement at the pump power of Fig. A2, not for each mode-selection experiment above. The paper names unwanted second harmonic and spontaneous parametric down conversion as possible noise sources but does not separate them.

assertions.value: The authors report visibilities of the photon counts of 0.9832 for the linear case (rotating the half-wave plate before the visible PBS) and 0.9804 for the nonlinear case (rotating the signal half-wave plate before the crystal), and state that this shows the system could be used for high-dimensional states in the polarization degree of freedom.
quotes: the visibility of the photon counts in linear and nonlinear cases are 0.9832 and 0.9804, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the use for polarization states is an author claim.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper calls these measurements preliminary; they test polarization dependence with classical counts, not polarization-encoded quantum states.
